# docker_compose_start (Action)

Starts the existing stopped containers of a compose project, like `docker compose start`. Containers are selected by the `com.docker.compose.project` and `com.docker.compose.service` labels (one-off `run` containers excluded), so projects made by `docker_compose` and by the CLI both work. The result lists each container's state afterwards (`result.container_states`).

Actions require Terraform 1.14 or later. An action keeps no state: it runs when
a resource's `lifecycle { action_trigger { events = [...] actions = [action.docker_compose_start.<name>] } }`
fires, or on demand with `terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_compose_start.<name>`.
Arguments go in the action's `config` block.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "docker_compose" "shop" {
  name    = "shop"
  content = <<-EOT
    services:
      web:
        image: nginx:1.27-alpine
        ports: ["8080:80"]
      worker:
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
  EOT

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, after_update]
      actions = [action.docker_compose_start.this]
    }
  }
}

# Starts the stopped containers of the project. Run it on demand with:
#   terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_compose_start.this
action "docker_compose_start" "this" {
  config {
    name = docker_compose.shop.name
  }
}
```

<!-- action schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The compose project name (`com.docker.compose.project` label, CLI `--project-name`).

### Optional

- `result_path` (String) Local file the action writes its result object to after a successful run. The file holds one JSON object keyed by the action's output names (`result`, the identity values, the raw outputs with their `*_sha256` hashes, and the version values), with keys sorted at every level, two-space indentation and a trailing newline; it is written atomically (temporary file, then rename) and parent directories are created. Read it in a later run with `jsondecode(file(...))` or the `local_file` data source. Sensitive values are written in full, since this is your own file, but show as `(sensitive)` in the progress message. Nothing is written when the action fails.
- `services` (List of String) Only these services (default: every service of the project).
